Following up after I pulled the AWS settlement report for Aug. Short summary: AWS posted a single payout to our seller account for all marketplace SKUs (subscription + metered). The settlement lines include AWS SKU IDs and gross amounts but no purchaser-entity coding on their payout side.

I've built a proposed SKU->Redwood-entity mapping (aws_sku_entity_map.csv attached). Proposed allocation logic:
- Use buyer account metadata (AWS buyer account ID + contract reference) where present to split metered usage line items
- For subscription SKUs tied to our consolidated listing, allocate by active contract lookup in Salesforce (salesforce SFIDs in column G)

Limitations: for ~12% of metered lines, buyer metadata is missing in the AWS export — we either ask AWS for a detailed allocation file or issue internal journal allocations and provide CloudCorp with a reconciliation report plus credit note to nullify double-taxation exposure.

I'm opening a support case with AWS to request a buyer-level allocation extract — copying their billing contact below. Case created: https://support.amazon.com/case/MP-987654321

Attachments: aws_sku_entity_map.csv

Next steps:
1) AWS/marketplace to confirm whether they can provide a buyer-allocation extract for the missing ~12% (I expect reply by EOD 9/18)
2) If AWS cannot, Redwood will prepare allocation file + credit note for CloudCorp (deliverable target 9/20)
3) Finance (Laura/Marissa) to confirm if a Redwood-origin credit note is acceptable for CloudCorp's ERP posting or if AWS must re-issue allocation credits on their statement.

-Markus
Manager, Marketplace Ops | Redwood Inference

- If enrichment fails, issue AWS-side credit notes to the buyer entity to align tax treatment (we can generate consolidated credit notes and provide accounting-level allocation files)
